newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index slips off high.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index slips off high.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, fell 0.1 percent to 311.29 at the start of play on Friday.
Latin America edged down 0.3 percent day-on-day to 584.05, Asia was down 0.1 percent at 259.89, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 0.4 percent at 143.30.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a 1997 high of 311.51 after the close of play on January 15.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was down 0.09 percent day-on-day at 169.83 at 0945 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a 1997 high of 169.99 after the close of play on January 15.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was up 1.04 percent at 505.602, calculated after the close of trade on Wednesday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. It touched a high last year of 505.452 on July 4, and recorded its 458.369 low on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.01 percent to 125.93 by the start of trade on Friday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was up 0.04 percent at 103.98, Asia fell 0.02 to 132.58 and East Europe was up 0.14 at 162.92. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
